required_configuration: worker_pids: nonempty explicit set of actual PHP-FPM pool worker PIDs
new_title: Application worker code paths are read-only
criterion: For every explicitly supplied PHP-FPM worker PID, the scanner and worker have identical effective UID/GID/groups, zero effective/permitted/ambient capabilities, matching project tree, mount namespace and Linux security context. Kernel access observations find no writable object or replaceable code root in the complete bounded configured app/vendor/lib inventory. Unsupported identity, seccomp, links or inventory gaps remain UNKNOWN.
limitations: Run scanner as the actual unprivileged worker identity; root or differing identity is unsupported rather than a violation.
All worker PIDs to be assessed must be explicitly supplied; no discovery-completeness claim.
Unsupported worker mode, nonzero seccomp filters, sticky parent rules, external links or missing /proc permissions yield UNKNOWN.
No code writes or privilege changes are performed.

new_title: Upload inventory has no configured PHP or handler signatures
criterion: Within the complete bounded configured upload path inventory, readable files contain no explicit long PHP opening tags or configured htaccess script-handler signatures and no PHP-like executable filename extension. Missing/unreadable/oversized eligible files, unfollowed links and traversal-budget gaps remain UNKNOWN. This is a signature policy, not absence of arbitrary executable content or prevention of server execution.
limitations: Default pub/media inventory is applicable without demanding absent optional import/export paths; explicitly add relevant roots.
Payload bytes and response bodies are never emitted; path/line/signature label only.
XML opening tags are not treated as PHP.
tests: tests/ProductionRuntimeCheckTest.php: benign XML, disguised PHP, oversized file, symlink, traversal budget and htaccess handler

limitations: Existing MB-0728 already resolves observed Admin password minimum declaration/installed validator minimum. Reuse it without adding duplicate coverage.
No new installed-validator acceptance adapter or support for arbitrary DI/plugins/IMS password policy was implemented in this unit.
tests: Existing MagentoConfigurationCompletionTest.php covers the active observed configuration predicate.

limitations: No bound denied-origin versus allowed-origin gateway adapter was implemented.
Repository ACL hints, route obscurity, HTTP 404 or lack of recognizable login markup are not accepted as restriction proof.

required_configuration: approved_role_ids: explicit positive integer role-ID array; [] explicitly means deny-all
new_title: Direct global Admin ACL grants match the approved role policy
criterion: In a nonempty bounded deployed authorization_role inventory and complete bounded authorization_rule inventory, every direct allow rule for Magento_Backend::all or Magento_Adminhtml::all assigned to a group role has a role ID in the explicitly configured approved_role_ids policy. Missing policy, malformed/orphan rows, direct user grants or incomplete tables remain UNKNOWN. This checks direct stored grants, not inherited effective privileges or business least privilege.
limitations: Reads actual database tables through env.php connection; test PDO injects a real in-memory database, not assertion rows.
No default approval list is invented; deployment owner must supply normal versioned policy configuration.
Native global-group predicate deliberately does not claim full effective ACL/plugin authorization.
tests: tests/ProductionRuntimeCheckTest.php: approved/unapproved real SELECT rows, absent versus explicit empty policy, orphan rows, no direct grants

limitations: Original PCI vendor-default-account evidence assessment is excluded from Magebean automation; no self-attestation file is accepted as protection proof.

new_title: Named checkout response emits the explicit enforced CSP baseline
criterion: The supplied checkout path returns a successful same-origin no-redirect HTTPS GET with one unambiguous enforced Content-Security-Policy. The emitted policy explicitly defines script-src, connect-src, frame-src, form-action, object-src and base-uri; assessed sources contain no wildcard, unsafe-inline, unsafe-eval or broad scheme-only source. object-src is exactly none, base-uri is exactly none or self, and reporting is present when configured. Report-only alone fails; redirect/inaccessible checkout, multiple policies, unsupported syntax or incomplete collection remain UNKNOWN.
limitations: A redirect because no cart/session exists is UNKNOWN, not missing-CSP FAIL.
Only named response is assessed; no checkout-wide or full browser execution guarantee.
No state-changing requests, login, purchase or retained cookie/body content.
Conservative explicit baseline can flag supported nonce plus unsafe-inline compatibility policy; title/criterion state exact Magebean policy, not universal CSP security judgment.
tests: tests/ProductionRuntimeCheckTest.php: exact policy, absent path, report-only, wildcard/unsafe-inline, duplicates, unsupported source syntax and off-origin response

criterion: One successful same-origin no-redirect HTTPS GET at the configured path emits exactly one X-Content-Type-Options header whose trimmed value is nosniff. Missing or invalid header on an observed successful response fails; duplicate headers, redirects, transport failures and incomplete collection remain UNKNOWN. HSTS and frame protection are assessed separately.
limitations: Nosniff plus existing HSTS/frame controls is not a claim of every security header on every route.
No source-file union is used; runtime headers are collected directly with peer verification and bounded memory.
tests: tests/ProductionRuntimeCheckTest.php: observed header, missing header, duplicates, redirect and malformed network path

new_title: Configured PHP-FPM workers have no mapped Xdebug binary module
criterion: Every explicitly inventoried Linux PHP-FPM worker is bound to its pool, executable identity and exact process start_ticks before and after a complete bounded nonempty /proc process-map observation. No Xdebug-named shared module is mapped in these verified workers. Missing or changed identity, empty/unreadable/truncated maps or malformed inventory remain UNKNOWN. This observes configured process mappings at scan time, not every deployment worker, Xdebug feature mode, statically linked code or complete PHP runtime settings.
limitations: Explicit process inventory is machine targeting configuration; it cannot assert a clean result. Process mappings are collected directly without reading environ or executing target PHP. Original historical criterion and ID remain in the engineering backlog; this new ID records only its exact supported observation.
No trusted web-worker effective display_errors telemetry adapter was implemented. Repository ini and a clean HTTP page remain insufficient.

new_title: Resolved native default-scope debug settings are disabled
criterion: Each explicitly named native debug configuration setting resolves through deployed env.php/config.php/default core_config_data or installed enabled-module defaults to a recognized disabled value in default scope. Any recognized enabled value fails; unavailable or malformed values remain UNKNOWN. Store-specific overrides, runtime environment and custom debug behavior are outside this predicate.
limitations: Reuse active MB-0729 rather than create a second default-debug requirement.
New method is an optional stricter resolved-value helper, not completed store-scope automation for original criterion.
tests: tests/ProductionRuntimeCheckTest.php: disabled, enabled with other unavailable paths and missing defaults

new_title: Resolved native default-scope debug settings are disabled
criterion: Same supported resolved default-scope predicate as MB-0740 implementation; reuse one observation and existing active MB-0729 rather than counting duplicate template-hint capabilities.
limitations: Complete active-store scope resolver and custom runtime override detection remain unimplemented.
tests: tests/ProductionRuntimeCheckTest.php: shared native debug helper fixtures

required_configuration: paths: explicit vendor-supported debug/verbose configuration paths for the installed integration versions
new_title: Named integration debug settings resolve disabled in default scope
criterion: Every explicitly configured integration debug/verbose setting path resolves through deployed env.php/config.php/default core_config_data or supported installed-module defaults to a recognized disabled value in default scope. Any recognized enabled value fails; omitted paths, missing values or unsupported flag representations remain UNKNOWN. This verifies named settings, not every third-party integration or store scope.
limitations: No heuristic debug/logging key regex and no inference that ordinary enabled audit logging is insecure.
Vendor path/version applicability must be provided as normal policy configuration; no invented universal vendor schema.
No default vendor list is shipped because repository does not contain authoritative installed integration schemas.
tests: tests/ProductionRuntimeCheckTest.php: mandatory path policy, debug off with ordinary logging on and malformed value
